main_body: Tall brick townhouse: slate mansard roof with a dormer and chimney, orange cornice, three storeys of brick wall with lit windows, an iron balcony and a green door
top_band: Slate roof slope in blue-grey with a lighter teal-grey flat deck above it, rows ~10-42 (about 30 rows). It ends at an orange cornice band at rows 42-46.
evidence: Down the middle column: slate roof surface (deck and tiled slope, rows 10-42), an orange cornice as the front-edge line (rows 42-46), a dark shadow row under it, then the brick front face. The front face is much taller than the roof and has stone window surrounds, sills, a balcony and a recessed door. The roof slope is large enough to read as a real top surface, as in the house references, so this is not a hat on a flat elevation. No receding side face.

style.evidence: Brick shows several tones with per-brick mortar and highlights. Slate tiles are shaded one by one. Window glass has panes and glow, and the stone trim has speckle. Outlines are dark brown, blue-grey or green, tinted by the neighbouring material, not pure black. There are no large flat areas, and the tile density matches or exceeds the references. It would sit next to the Beodeul houses without looking thinner.
